declared_purpose: Search existing agent memory using semantic vectors when available and keyword fallback otherwise; retrieve requested file content, sync an index, and report status. Sync is explicitly optional (SKILL.md:8–12,23–28,47–65). The packaged local paths are auditable; the referenced pgvector implementation and external dependency behavior remain unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Read existing memory for keyword search and return ranked snippets.
data_operations.source: MEMORY.md and immediate .md children of memory/ under OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE or the default workspace.
data_operations.data_scope: Entire selected files are read locally. Matching lines receive surrounding context, truncated to 300 characters per result.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: smart_memory.js process; ranked paths, line references, scores and snippets return to its caller or CLI stdout.
data_operations.condition: Vector readiness fails, vector execution fails, or vector search returns no results. The memory/ directory must be enumerable; this fallback does not recurse into documented subdirectories.

data_operations.operation: Read memory and derive semantic embeddings locally through the imported model library.
data_operations.source: Hardcoded /config/.openclaw/workspace/MEMORY.md and immediate .md children of its memory/ directory.
data_operations.data_scope: Full files are read and hashed, then split into chunks. Only the first 500 characters of each chunk are supplied for embedding. These vectors represent text semantics; no separate preference or personality classifier is shown.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: vector_memory_local.js memory and the imported @xenova/transformers pipeline; subsequent index storage is separate.
data_operations.condition: Explicit sync, installer-triggered sync, or an adopted heartbeat/cron sync instruction. Nested memory directories are not traversed.

data_operations.operation: Persist an index and replace previously indexed records for each visited file.
data_operations.source: Existing index and newly processed memory chunks.
data_operations.data_scope: Full chunk plaintext, embeddings, source paths, line offsets, whole-file MD5 hashes, model metadata and last-sync time. Existing records for a visited path are removed before embedding replacements.
data_operations.condition: Sync loads the existing database and saves it after processing currently discovered files. There is no general purge of records belonging to undiscovered files.

data_operations.operation: Embed a query, infer relevance scores, reread selected source files and return results.
data_operations.source: Caller query, saved embeddings and selected original memory files.
data_operations.data_scope: The full query is embedded; all indexed chunks receive cosine scores. Results above 0.3 are ranked and may be merged. Selected source files are read fully, then requested ranges produce snippets of up to 500 characters plus an ellipsis.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local vector process and model pipeline. Direct vector CLI stdout includes the query and results; smart_memory.js and memory.js return only mapped result fields to their callers.
data_operations.condition: Direct vector search or memory.js search; the default smart wrapper attempts this only when its readiness check succeeds. No query-vector persistence is shown.

data_operations.operation: Read a caller-selected file and return a line slice.
data_operations.source: file_path joined to the smart wrapper's workspace.
data_operations.data_scope: The whole resolved file is read locally; only the selected lines are returned. Invalid or absent numeric arguments default to line 1 and 50 lines.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: smart_memory.js process and its caller or CLI stdout; no persistence is shown.
data_operations.condition: memory_get targets smart_memory.js. Targets are checked for existence but are not restricted to memory sources. The legacy memory.js version uses require inside a packaged ES module, so its caught failure should not be counted as a successful read path.

data_operations.operation: Read index contents to check readiness and report metadata.
data_operations.data_scope: The complete JSON database is parsed. Smart status returns readiness, chunk count, last-sync time and workspace path; direct vector status returns status, model, count and sync time.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local processes; metadata returns to the caller or stdout.
data_operations.condition: Smart searches perform readiness checks; status commands perform metadata checks. Smart status reads a ready database again after its readiness check.

data_operations.operation: Write query and indexing diagnostics to standard error.
data_operations.source: Search query, indexed source paths, chunk counts, database path and caught errors.
data_operations.data_scope: The vector backend prints the complete query before embedding it and prints source paths while syncing.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Process stderr. External collection, forwarding and persistence are not established.
data_operations.condition: Vector search with a nonempty index; sync progress and error paths produce additional diagnostics.

data_operations.operation: Initialize a model pipeline and cache model assets.
data_operations.data_scope: A quantized feature-extraction model; the source documents an approximately 80 MB first-run download. Memory chunks and queries are passed to the resulting pipeline.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured local cache at /config/.openclaw/workspace/.cache/transformers. Download recipients and dependency behavior are unspecified in supplied source.
data_operations.condition: An embedding is requested; the pipeline is reused within the process. The supplied code contains no explicit remote memory-upload request.

data_operations.operation: Download installation source and dependencies, then copy package files locally.
data_operations.source: The installer's GitHub repository endpoint and npm dependency installation.
data_operations.data_scope: Repository and dependency requests and downloaded code. No memory-file payload is specified in these acquisition commands.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: GitHub endpoint named by REPO_URL; npm recipients are unspecified. Downloads use /tmp, with package copies placed in the detected OpenClaw workspace.
data_operations.condition: install.sh is selected and prerequisites succeed; git clone or tarball download is chosen according to git availability.

data_operations.source: Temporary repository checkout or extracted archive directory.
data_operations.data_scope: The git branch removes its named temporary directory before cloning and after copying; the tarball branch removes its extracted directory after copying.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local /tmp filesystem. This cleanup does not delete memory files, vector records or model cache.
data_operations.condition: The corresponding install.sh branch reaches each removal command.

data_operations.operation: Run installation-time indexing and optional diagnostic searches.
data_operations.source: Existing memory selected by the vector backend or smart wrapper.
data_operations.data_scope: install.sh unconditionally invokes sync after dependency installation. The separate --test command searches existing memory using fixed sample queries and prints counts, method and, on the vector branch, a top-match path and score.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Index storage for installer sync; diagnostic stdout and vector-query stderr for tests.
data_operations.condition: Successful installer progression, or explicit invocation of --test. Diagnostic searches can read real memory but do not print its snippets in the test branch.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full chunk plaintext, including text beyond the 500 characters embedded, and repeated whole-file MD5 hashes.
potential_excess.condition: Successful chunk indexing and database save.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Semantic indexing is required when sync is selected. Duplicating full source plaintext and unused hashes is an implementation choice within that required action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain embeddings and source-location metadata sufficient for scoring and retrieving matching source ranges.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit cached plaintext and unused hashes; remove cached-content concatenation during merging. Continue fetching result text from original files, as the CLI already does.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve embeddings, paths, line offsets, ranking and merged range calculations so search results remain available.

potential_excess.data_scope: Previously indexed plaintext, embeddings, hashes and paths for deleted, renamed or otherwise no-longer-discovered memory files.
potential_excess.condition: Sync loads an existing index after a source disappears from the enumerated corpus. Only visited paths have old records removed.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Sync is intended to index current memory after edits. Retaining absent sources is additional persistence, even though missing originals are suppressed when results are fetched.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Maintain a searchable index of current eligible memory sources.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Before saving, prune records whose paths are absent from the current eligible source set.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Distinguish confirmed removal from enumeration failure; preserve records for current eligible files. This narrows logical retention without claiming secure physical erasure.

potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: vector_memory_local.js stderr; downstream retention is unknown.
potential_excess.condition: A vector search proceeds with a nonempty index.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The query is necessary for embedding and ranking. Printing it is a redundant diagnostic action, separate from returning search results to the caller.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Consume the query for local semantic search.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the raw-query diagnostic or replace it with a generic search-progress message.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep query embedding, scoring and normal result returns unchanged.

potential_excess.data_scope: Accessible files outside the intended memory corpus, potentially outside the workspace through parent-directory traversal.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: smart_memory.js process for the full-file read; the calling agent or CLI stdout for the requested line slice.
potential_excess.condition: memory_get receives a path resolving outside approved memory sources, and the resolved file exists and is readable.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared tool retrieves memory-file content. Existence checking alone permits a broader source scope than that purpose requires; this is conditional local access and caller disclosure, not demonstrated remote exfiltration.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve requested line ranges from legitimate memory files, including organized memory subdirectories.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Validate resolved targets against approved memory files and directories before reading.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Allow legitimate nested memory notes and requested ranges while rejecting targets escaping approved roots.

potential_excess.data_scope: Existing memory files and their derived persistent index, plus model-cache acquisition.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local vector backend, vectors_local.json and model cache.
potential_excess.condition: install.sh reaches its unconditional initial sync after installing dependencies.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry document explicitly makes sync optional and promises immediate keyword fallback. Automatic installation-time indexing adds an action beyond basic installation.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Install the skill and dependencies so fallback search can operate.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Defer indexing to an explicit memory_sync invocation or an installation option selecting sync.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep explicit sync available and preserve semantic search after it is selected.

unknowns: The optional pgvector branch remains unaudited: vector_memory.js and docker-compose.yml are absent. Documentation names PostgreSQL and OpenAI embeddings, but actual submitted text, recipients, database persistence and deletion cannot be established. Credential identifiers include PG_PASSWORD and OPENAI_API_KEY (vector-memory/references/pgvector.md:3–29,50–55).

The @xenova/transformers implementation is absent. Model-download hosts, additional network behavior, telemetry and cache cleanup cannot be verified; the packaged local-inference claim alone does not establish those external behaviors (vector-memory/package.json:7–9; vector-memory/vector_memory_local.js:27–50,302).

ClawHub installation, npm internals and the OpenClaw command runner are not supplied. Their request contents, argument handling and retention of tool calls, stdout or stderr remain unknown; ordinary results are only established as returning to their caller (SKILL.md:16–21; install.sh:68; skills/vector-memory/skill.json:8–10,25–27).

Alternate-workspace behavior is inconsistent: smart_memory.js honors OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE, while the vector backend uses hardcoded paths. SKILL.md advertises MEMORY_DIR and MEMORY_FILE overrides that the backend does not read. The intended corpus under such configuration remains unresolved (SKILL.md:108–117; vector-memory/smart_memory.js:16,95–104; vector-memory/vector_memory_local.js:19–21).
